name: Diplodocus
sum: Diplodocus is a well-known diplodocid sauropod with a very long neck and whip-like tail from the Late Jurassic of North America.
wsnote: Revised length estimate for the largest species, D. hallorum, in the cited Wikipedia revision; smaller species are shorter (for example a 29 m D. carnegii in one estimate).
holotype: Not read in the sources consulted; the first fossils were found in 1877 by S. W. Williston and the genus was named by Marsh in 1878.
material: One of the more common dinosaur fossils of the middle to upper Morrison Formation, mostly from rocks about 151.9–149.1 Ma.
biology: Named for its double-beamed chevron bones; in a tripodal posture it could perhaps raise its feeding height to about 11 m.
author: Marsh 1878
